title: Imperfect vs. Preterite
description: Understand when to use the imperfect versus the preterite — the key decision point for Spanish past tenses.

vocabulary.source: I was studying / used to study
I was working / used to work

grammar.title: Imperfect vs. Preterite: When to Use Which
grammar.content:
This is the key decision point for A2.1 learners. The preterite (from A1.2) and imperfect both describe the past, but differently.

Use IMPERFECT for:
- Habitual/repeated actions: 'De niño, nadaba todos los días.' (As a kid, I swam every day.)
- Ongoing background descriptions: 'Era una noche oscura y tormentosa.' (It was a dark and stormy night.)
- Age, time, weather in the past: 'Tenía 20 años. Eran las tres. Llovía.' (I was 20. It was three o'clock. It was raining.)
- Feelings and emotions in the past: 'Era feliz. Estaba cansado.' (I was happy. I was tired.)

Use PRETERITE for:
- Completed actions with a start/end: 'Ayer hablé con mi jefe.' (Yesterday I talked with my boss.)
- A series of completed actions: 'Me levanté, me duché y salí.' (I got up, showered, and left.)
- One-time specific past events: 'El año pasado fui a Italia.' (Last year I went to Italy.)

rows: Fue alto y rubio (described him as such)

examples: Cuando era niño, jugaba al fútbol. Todos los días. (When I was a child, I used to play soccer. Every day.)
Ayer jugué al fútbol. Ganamos 3-0. (Yesterday I played soccer. We won 3-0.)
Mientras ella cocinaba, él lavó los platos. (While she was cooking, he washed the dishes.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian also distinguishes between imperfect and aorist/preterite, but the distinction is less strictly taught in modern usage. The key intuition: imperfect = 'used to do / was doing', preterite = 'did (once, completed)'. In Romanian: 'făceam' (imperfect) vs 'făcei' (aorist/preterite).

exercises.question: Which tense would you use for a repeated past action?
exercises.explanation: The imperfect is used for repeated/habitual past actions: 'Cada verano viajábamos a Italia.'

exercises.question: Which tense would you use for a one-time completed action?
exercises.explanation: The preterite is used for completed actions: 'Ayer viajamos a Italia.'

exercises.question: Complete: 'De niño, yo ____ (leer) muchos libros.' (As a child, I used to read many books.)
exercises.explanation: 'Leía' — imperfect for a repeated/habitual childhood action.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ayer ____ (yo) ____ (ir) al cine.' (Yesterday I went to the cinema.)
exercises.explanation: 'Fui' — preterite of ir for a one-time completed action.

exercises.question: Which sentence pairs the imperfect and preterite correctly?
options: Mientras llovía, estaba sonando el teléfono.
exercises.explanation: 'Mientras llovía (imperfect/background), sonó el teléfono (preterite/interrupting action).' This is the classic imperfect + preterite combination.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Eran las ____ (three). ____ (It was) una noche oscura.'
exercises.explanation: 'Eran las tres' (time uses imperfect of ser) and 'Hacía' (weather description uses imperfect of hacer). Both are background descriptions.
